correctness.rationale: For all k>=2 and h>=1 the proof reduces EJR-1 under the explicit project-approval pattern to singleton private-bundle and joint-common-project constraints. Necessity and sufficiency are proved separately for both utilities, with strict augmentation, exact budget accounting, all coalition sizes and nonexhaustive outcomes. Binomial cost-outcome count and private-bundle deficit follow constructively. Direct enumeration of 63,191 feasible outcomes across 13 parameter pairs independently matched all formulae; finite tests are not used as the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The paper-initiating result demonstrates incompatibility for one (k,h)=(2,5) example. The present claim supplies a necessary-and-sufficient full equilibrium-like fairness spectrum for every integer k>=2,h>=1, a unique cardinal-fair allocation above a sharp premium boundary, an exact cost-fair count, and a sharp cost-fair private-bundle deficit. It is not implied by the published existential witness or single-objective algorithmic guarantees. Current literature and indexed findings were searched by claims and aliases; possible recent uninspected precedence is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Later specialist results, including full texts of arXiv:2609.02030 and arXiv:2610.15516, were not conclusively compared. Priority uncertainty is nonzero.
Semantic database searches and accessible historical records cannot establish uniqueness over unindexed or unpublished work.
The initiating two-voter counterexample is known; novelty is claimed only for the complete parameterized classification, exact counting and sharp quantitative threshold.

value.rationale: The result closes a natural two-tier public-versus-local budget model motivated by an established incompatibility example. Unlike a routine numeric replacement, it supplies complete structural iff tests, a sharp premium-to-voter-number compatibility threshold, an exact spectrum count, and a quantitative optimal private-representation shortfall under cost-EJR-1. It formalizes the price of competing cardinal/cost proportionality measures in a family of arbitrary population size, enabling exact analysis and direct feasibility testing.
